equivalent.reason: Net::HTTPHeader#[] looks the field up by key.downcase, so both spellings return the same header value.
String.new without arguments already returns an empty ASCII-8BIT (BINARY) string: same object state.
The block body is the single expression; or and || differ only in precedence against assignment, and there is none, so the block value is identical.
Agent#display_name is always defined, so try only differs from &. on nil receivers, where both give nil.
Hash#[] and fetch(key, nil) return the same value for present and missing keys (no default proc on default_url_options).
URI.parse returns a URI::Generic (or subclass), which always defines host, so try(:host) is a plain call.
